To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the feature selection methods are not suitable for cost modelling, but the wrapper methods are more effective than the filter and embedded ones.
feature subset selection is not always beneficial and it depends on the nature of the dataset, and that the wrapper method outperforms the filter methods.

the wrapper-based feature selection methods outperform filter-based methods, that the best performing wrapper method was CFS, and that CFS outperformed other methods in terms of accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What are the most informative attributes in the datasets? What are the most suitable subset selection methods? How can we improve the performance of cost models using feature subset selection?

the following issues: (i) the appropriateness and suitability of the feature selection methods in the area of cost estimation, (ii) the impact of the selected features on the performance of the estimation models, (iii) the impact of feature selection on the robustness of the estimation models.

the following questions: (i) How can feature subset selection be used in the area software cost estimation? (ii) What is the impact of feature selection on the accuracy of software cost estimation? and (iii) What is the best feature subset selection method for the software cost estimation problem?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
feature selection methods are not always appropriate for software cost modelling and estimation.
there is no one single method that is superior to all others in terms of the accuracy and the robustness.

feature selection is not an effective technique for improving the accuracy of software cost models, and the use of a feature selection technique should be considered only if it is necessary to reduce the number of features in the dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wrapper methods outperform the filter approaches and that a combination of filter and wrapper methods can be used to obtain the best subset selection.
the wrapper methods are superior to other methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
the feature selection methods used in this work have been shown to improve the performance of the cost models in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the wrapper methods outperformed filter approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness.
there is no one-size-fits-all feature selection technique.
the performance of feature selection techniques is not always directly related to the number of features used in the model.
